description: Which server process answers HTTP requests, which one executes background jobs, how are they started, how do they relate through shared infrastructure, and what is observable if the job-executing process is absent?
anchor_note: non-bug task: root_cause_symbols holds the anchor (entry point / changed symbol); RC metrics are reported for category A only

source.verification: Static reading; queue.service.spec.ts does not cover onBootstrap (UNVERIFIED). No test found for checkWorkers.
source.notes: Workers.bootstrap/startWorker are class members of a non-exported class in main.ts (lines 14-). 'bootstrap' in workers/maintenance.ts is a module-level function, not a class member. Redis (BullMQ) and Postgres are the only shared media.

evidence: server/src/main.ts:22-35 Workers.bootstrap, :90-110 startWorker (fork for API :100, worker thread :108)
server/src/repositories/job.repository.ts:90-99 startWorkers (worker name microservices :97), :102-104 watchWorkers, :115-135 checkWorkers (30 s, warning text)

notes: Verified: Workers.bootstrap (main.ts:22-35) starts each enabled worker; startWorker forks API (child process) and runs others as worker threads (:90-110); AppBootstrap -> QueueService.onBootstrap starts BullMQ Workers in Microservices (job.repository.ts:90-99) and the API runs watchWorkers/checkWorkers every interval, which warns "No microservices worker is connected. Background jobs will not be processed" (job.repository.ts:121-145).

Missing the per-process entry points that answer HTTP vs run jobs: src/workers/api.ts::bootstrap (:9, listens HTTP) and src/workers/microservices.ts::bootstrap (:12, app.listen(0) for socket.io only), and JobRepository.queueAll (shared Redis/BullMQ queue written by the API).
